summary: Frontend-only testing of the new mobile floating filter bar, drawer taxonomy selects, accordion defaults, and back-scroll restore on Encar (BG). Verified 12/13 items in the request; 1 critical regression found: back-scroll restore does NOT return to the previous offset (lands ~927px short both via header-back-button and browser go_back). All other mobile floating-bar behaviours (hidden at top, appears when in-page Филтри leaves top, full-width white 44px flush bar with -1 header overlap, red dot when filters active, drawer opens, header menu button remains clickable while bar visible), drawer taxonomy selects (make/model/badge visible; changing make in the drawer updates the URL to English slug make=kia and persists after close), accordion defaults (price/year/mileage=open; fuel/transmission/region/documents=closed; fuel still opens and its checkboxes still update the URL to fuels=petrol), and desktop 1920x900 regression (floating bar hidden, taxonomy selects present, no drawer) all pass.

ui_bugs.issue: After navigating from car detail back to the list, the page is left at scrollY≈1273 instead of the recorded 2200 (delta ~927px, well beyond the ~150px tolerance). Reproduced BOTH via [data-testid=header-back-button] on mobile and via page.go_back() (browser back gesture). Root cause is almost certainly the restore effect at SearchPage.js:100-105 firing on the very first render where result.items.length>0: window.scrollTo(0, target) runs before card images/rows have laid out, so the document is still shorter than the target and the browser clamps the offset. Once images finish loading the height grows to well past 2200 but the scroll has already stopped at ~1273 and is never re-applied. Fix: retry the scroll on subsequent layout changes (e.g. ResizeObserver on the results container, or a couple of rAF-delayed reapplications) until document.documentElement.scrollHeight >= target+viewport, then clear restoreTo.current.

data-testid="filter-sidebar" is rendered TWICE on mobile at the same time: once by the desktop-only container (hidden with lg:block but still present in the DOM behind a hidden ancestor) and once inside the mobile <SheetContent>. This trips Playwright strict-mode selectors and makes it impossible to uniquely target the drawer without scoping to role=dialog. Recommend giving the sheet copy a distinct testid such as filter-sidebar-sheet.

Desktop back button uses data-testid="back-to-results" (no -button suffix), which does not match the naming convention used elsewhere (car-card-details-button, header-back-button, floating-filters-button, open-filters-button). Not a functional bug – the button works – but tests referring to back-to-results-button (as in the review request) will silently miss it.

integration_issues.issue: Both mobile in-app back (header-back-button) and browser back gesture leave the list at scrollY 1273 instead of 2200. The list URL and applied filters (?make=hyundai) are correctly preserved – only the scroll offset regresses.

action_items: Fix scroll restore in SearchPage.js: reapply window.scrollTo until the results container is tall enough for the target offset (ResizeObserver or a bounded rAF retry loop). Currently ~927px short on both header-back and browser go_back.
Deduplicate data-testid="filter-sidebar" – rename the mobile sheet copy to filter-sidebar-sheet (or scope the desktop one to lg-only rendering) so the drawer can be selected unambiguously.
Rename data-testid="back-to-results" to data-testid="back-to-results-button" for naming consistency and to match the review request.
critical_code_review_comments: SearchPage.js restore effect runs once on loading→false with items>0 but does not wait for image/lazy layout to settle; a single scrollTo is fragile whenever the target offset is beyond the initial content height.

The floating bar wrapper stays in the DOM at all times with pointer-events-none + opacity-0 when hidden. That's intentional (transition), but note is_visible() from Playwright will report True; tests must key on wrap opacity or use pointer-events, not is_visible.

TaxonomySelects uses a native <select>, so any Playwright test that tries page.get_by_role('option').click() will fail on mobile Chromium – tests must use locator.select_option(value=…). Worth documenting for future test agents.

success_rate.frontend: ~85% (12 of 13 explicit checks pass; scroll restore fails)

test_credentials: admin@encarskin.com / <ADMIN_SEED_PASSWORD from backend/.env> (not exercised – all tested flows were anonymous)
context_for_next_testing_agent: Live catalogue counts on this run: hyundai=38 866, kia=37 890. Mobile viewport 390x844 must be set AFTER first paint (harness ignores it before navigate). The floating bar only becomes interactive (wrapOpacity=1) once scrollY ≳ 1300 on the current layout – measurements: scrollY 0/500 -> wrapOpacity 0; scrollY 1400/2500/4000 -> wrapOpacity 1, fb.top=-1, header collapsed to top=-65. Bar geometry left=0 width=390 height=44 radius=0 bg=rgb(255,255,255). Dot present when make=hyundai. To change the make from inside the drawer use `dialog.locator('[data-testid=taxonomy-make-select]').select_option(value='기아')` – the native <select> option value is the Korean string; the resulting URL uses the English slug make=kia. Fuel section testid is on the AccordionTrigger button itself so clicking `[data-testid=filter-section-fuel]` directly toggles it. Fuel option checkboxes carry testid=filter-fuel-option. Desktop 1920x900: floating bar wrapper computed display=none, one taxonomy-selects, zero dialogs, back link is data-testid=back-to-results (no -button).
rca of the issue: Reproduction: on /bg/?make=hyundai (mobile 390x844) scroll to 2200, tap first car-card-details-button, land on /bg/car/<id>, tap header-back-button. Expected scrollY≈2200, actual 1273 (delta 927). Same result via page.go_back(). Cause: SearchPage.js:100-105 runs `window.scrollTo(0, target)` as soon as loading=false and items>0, but the results grid still has un-laid-out card thumbnails, so document.scrollHeight is smaller than target+viewport and the browser clamps the scroll. Once images finish loading the extra height is added but the restore effect has already cleared restoreTo.current and won't retry. Mitigation: wrap the scroll in a bounded rAF/ResizeObserver retry that keeps scrolling until document.documentElement.scrollHeight >= target + window.innerHeight (or a max of ~1s / 30 frames), then null out restoreTo.current.
